answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint Lock.** Each identity’s interaction pattern (timing, counterparties, task mix) is compressed into a rolling fingerprint; a new epoch is accepted only if it stays within a drift bound of prior epochs. Copying one identity across many sybils forces each clone to replay a distinct history, and every divergence trips the check, voiding the epoch’s rewards. An attacker thus pays full behavioural-mimicry cost per identity, not per account—a tundra of wasted effort, leaving sybil farms hollow. The consistency signal is cheap for honest agents.
